integrity: The proof uses a bijection from half-graph edges to pairs of an ordered (n+1)-set. Any triangle in the image yields three selected edges on a length-three geodesic, so Mantel gives the sharp upper bound. Equality in Mantel forces a balanced complete bipartite image, and the edge-general-position condition is then exactly the absence of a four-run alternating color subsequence. This proves the value, all maxima, and their count.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats twin-free half graphs rather than arbitrary chain graphs with repeated twin classes.
Finite exhaustive verification proves only the checked finite cases and is corroborative for the all-orders theorem.
A differently phrased or non-indexed half-graph treatment may exist.
The 2026 graph-product paper was compared through accessible abstract and bibliographic scope rather than full text.
title: Edge general position sets of half graphs via Mantel's theorem
